Edit: As for something I'd like to happen in my lifetime, I'd like to see a return to prosperity for all in America (I'd like it for the world too, but don't know much about international economic history). I'd like to see single-income families thrive again. Middle-class neighborhoods where a banker lives next door to a cop, who lives next door to a master carpenter, who lives next door to a nurse, who lives next door to a career enlisted man. Where everybody gets an honest day's pay for an honest day's work. And we quit sending so many jobs overseas and siphoning profits up to the top floors and to shareholders. And we make things again in america. And you don't need a college education for a well-paying job, especially if you enter a trade or area of technical specialization. Basically I'd like us to turn into a less-racist, less-sexist 1950s economic america, I guess.

I'd like to see the full automation of the work force. It would be interesting to see what happens when no-one needs to work at a McDonalds for there to be McDonalds.

Will we all just sit around and be pampered by machines, start a society based on poetry and other artistic endeavors?

Every time this automation thing gets brought up people get really scared, and think their jobs will be lost, and it will ruin the whole economy, and Jesus will come down, and shoot everyone with a machine gun.

Yes, things will change, but it's not going to be a huge disaster. The paradigm of how people make a living will change.

  • A lot of jobs will be in robotics, computers, and programming. They will replace some of the jobs that are inevitably lost. There will be those who have to maintain these systems as well.

  • Certain jobs just won't die, no matter what, because some people simply prefer face to face interactions. At the bank, for example, despite the introduction of automatic transaction machines, most people will speak to a teller.

  • More people will be self-employed. This is what automation will create. We will have a lot of small companies, and small businesses popping up. At the point automation technology become so cheap that every business can afford it, then that means it will be accessible to the ordinary man. For example, suppose you want to make a product -- you might 3D print it in your home, pack it up, and have it sent out via self-driving car or truck. Or you might have a plot of land, and have a machine grow vegetables for you, and then you can eat that, and sell the excess. There are a ton of possibilities here.
